title: Fahrenheit Symbol: Copy & Paste ℉ Degree Fahrenheit Sign
meta_description: Copy and paste the degree Fahrenheit sign (℉, U+2109) — the single-character temperature ligature, why Unicode recommends plain °F, and how to type it on Windows and Mac. Click any symbol to copy it.
hero_tagline: ℉ folds the degree sign and a capital F into one Unicode character — quick to paste, though most style guides still prefer the two-character °F. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
intro: The degree Fahrenheit sign (℉, Unicode U+2109) is a precomposed character in the Letterlike Symbols block combining the degree sign (°) with a capital F. Like its Celsius counterpart ℃, it was added to Unicode largely for lossless round-tripping of legacy East Asian text, where a temperature reading often filled a single character cell. In everyday writing the recommended form is the degree sign followed by a plain F (°F), but the single ℉ is the fastest glyph to copy when that is all you need.
